home-remodeling.meta_description: 1920s cottages and mid-century ranches in Victoria Park, Fort Lauderdale, gutted and rebuilt with city permits. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.h1: Keep the cottage, rebuild everything else
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Full-gut and whole-home remodels for Victoria Park's 1920s cottages, Mediterranean Revivals and mid-century ranches. Permitted through Fort Lauderdale Development Services, inspected under Broward's building code, and run daily by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Victoria Park was platted in 1925 and filled in over the next three decades, which is why one block can hold a Mission-style cottage, a Craftsman bungalow, a small Mediterranean Revival and a low-slung mid-century ranch. The lots are modest, the streets curve, and the oak canopy is the reason people pay what they pay. Almost nobody scrapes these houses. Instead they gut them: the front elevation stays, the interior walls come out, the ceilings open up, and a 1938 floor plan finally gets a great room, real closets and a primary suite.

Plan review and permitting sit with the City of Fort Lauderdale Development Services Department, filed online in LauderBuild. Behind the city sits the county: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which administers the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies building officials and inspectors, and issues formal code interpretations. Broward is also inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every impact window, door and roofing assembly needs HVHZ product approval. Victoria Park is not one of the city's three historic districts, but an individually designated landmark still needs a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Board.

Our people have been building in South Florida for more than 20 years, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered and every one permitted and inspected. On a street this narrow, that record matters less than conduct: one dumpster where it belongs, deliveries that do not block your neighbor's driveway, and crews that keep to the city's construction hours. You get a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site every working day, floors and millwork protected, and a single accountable team from the first estimate through final inspection and warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: What we touch in a cottage gut
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing is priced by guess. Here is what a whole-home remodel in Victoria Park usually contains once we have walked the house and read the original plans.

scope_items.name: Taking out the walls
scope_items.desc: Removing partitions between kitchen, dining and living, with steel or engineered beams sized by an engineer and permitted before anything structural comes down.

scope_items.name: Everything behind the plaster
scope_items.desc: New panel and service, copper or PEX in place of galvanized, cast iron drains replaced, and ductwork designed for a house that once had none.

scope_items.name: HVHZ impact openings
scope_items.desc: Impact windows and doors with Broward-accepted HVHZ approvals, detailed in profiles and sightlines that suit a 1930s elevation instead of flattening it.

scope_items.name: Framing, termites and rot
scope_items.desc: Wood-framed cottages get opened, inspected and repaired properly: sistered joists, replaced sheathing, treated framing and tie-downs brought up to current code.

scope_items.name: Millwork and finishes
scope_items.desc: Custom cabinetry, casings and baseboards scaled to the original ceiling heights, plus stone, tile and paint sequenced so nothing gets installed twice.

faqs.q: Is Victoria Park a historic district? Do I need special approval to remodel?
faqs.a: No, the neighborhood is not one of Fort Lauderdale's designated historic districts, so there is no district-wide design board reviewing your elevation. Individually designated landmark properties are the exception: those need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city's Historic Preservation Board before exterior work. Most Victoria Park remodels go straight to Development Services for plan review. We check your property's status in the first week, not the week before demolition.

faqs.q: Broward has a Board of Rules and Appeals. What does it do?
faqs.a: Indirectly, and constantly. Broward runs a countywide code layer above every city building department. The Board of Rules and Appeals adopts the county's administrative amendments to the Florida Building Code, sets the certification standards your building official and inspectors must hold, and hears appeals and formal interpretations when a code section is disputed. You will never file anything with them. Your contractor should know the Broward amendments cold, because Fort Lauderdale inspectors enforce them.

faqs.q: Does the Victoria Park Civic Association have to approve my remodel?
faqs.a: No. The VPCA is a voluntary civic association, not a homeowners association, and it has no architectural review power over your permit. What it does have is a long record of showing up at City Hall on zoning and development questions, and a membership that notices a job site immediately. That is a reason to run a clean, quiet, well-signed project, not a reason to fear it. Good neighbors are cheaper than complaint calls.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take here?
faqs.a: Design and permitting come first, and on an older Fort Lauderdale house they take months rather than weeks once engineering, survey and plan review comments are in. Construction on a full gut of a two- to three-thousand-square-foot cottage generally runs the better part of a year. Structural changes, second-floor work and long-lead cabinetry stretch it. We hand you a written schedule with the estimate and then defend it with daily supervision.

faqs.q: What should a whole-home remodel in Victoria Park cost?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on how deep you go, and anyone quoting a per-square-foot number over the phone is guessing. A cosmetic refresh and a full gut with new electrical, plumbing, HVAC, impact glass and structural openings are different projects with different budgets. We scope in writing, with allowances tied to real selections, so the number you sign is the number that holds. PGX builds at the high end and prices accordingly, and we would rather say that up front than discover it together later.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the plans, the wish list, or just the frustration. You will leave with a fixed scope and a schedule for the cottage, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodels for Victoria Park, FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Victoria Park kitchen remodeling in Fort Lauderdale. The old service galley becomes a room, cabinetry and stone included. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: Cook where the pantry used to be
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for Victoria Park kitchens, permitted through the City of Fort Lauderdale, inspected at every stage, and supervised on site by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Where the service kitchen used to be
intro_paragraphs: The kitchens in Victoria Park's older houses are almost all in the wrong place. A 1930s cottage off North Victoria Park Road put the kitchen at the back corner, behind a swinging door, with a window over the sink and barely room for two people. The mid-century ranches nearer Holiday Park did better and still landed a galley. So the real kitchen remodeling project on these blocks is spatial: swallow the breakfast nook or the old service porch, take down the wall to the dining room, and put an island where the pantry stood.

Kitchen permits go through Fort Lauderdale Building Services, filed in LauderBuild, with separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections carried out by inspectors certified under the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. Two Victoria Park realities show up early. Many of these houses still carry undersized electrical service that will not run an induction range, a wall oven and a wine unit at once. And the city has been replacing the neighborhood's original two-inch water mains with six- and eight-inch mains, which is worth knowing before you blame a new faucet for weak pressure.

We order cabinetry before demolition and template stone after the boxes are set, which sounds obvious until you have lived through the reverse. Your kitchen gets a fixed written scope, a supervisor here every working day, and dust walls that keep drywall grit out of the rest of a house you already finished. Deliveries are staged so nobody on the street loses a parking space for a month. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, 150-plus remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected. Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Selections and structure both get written down before the first cabinet is ordered. These five items carry most of the budget on these blocks.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry made to fit
scope_items.desc: Cabinet packages built to your dimensions and finished for coastal humidity, with interiors planned around how you actually store things, not a standard box list.

scope_items.name: The wall that goes
scope_items.desc: Engineered beams and posts where the kitchen wall used to be, with load calculations sealed, permitted and inspected before the drywall closes.

scope_items.name: Islands and stone
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain slabs templated on set cabinets, with overhangs carried on steel and seams placed where you will not be looking at them.

scope_items.name: Appliances that move
scope_items.desc: Relocating range, refrigeration and dishwasher where the new plan wants them, with dedicated circuits, water lines and exterior-vented hoods permitted as part of the job.

scope_items.name: Service, panel and light
scope_items.desc: Upgraded electrical service and panel where the old one cannot cope, plus layered lighting on separate controls instead of one fixture in the middle.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: For a real kitchen, yes. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, changing venting or touching structure all require permits filed through LauderBuild, plus inspections at rough and final. Painting and swapping a dishwasher into existing hookups do not. Unpermitted kitchen work in Victoria Park has a habit of surfacing at closing, when a buyer's inspector counts outlets that never appeared on a card. Legalizing after the fact costs more and looks worse.

faqs.q: Can I get gas for a range in Victoria Park?
faqs.a: Not everywhere, so check before you fall in love with a particular range. Natural gas service is not universal across these blocks, and we confirm what is actually at the property line rather than assuming. Where a main is not available, a permitted propane tank is often the practical route, and plenty of clients simply move to induction and never look back. Either path needs its own permit and its own inspection.

faqs.q: Will my old house handle a modern appliance package?
faqs.a: Often not without help. Houses built here in the thirties and forties were wired for a refrigerator, a light and a radio, and many still run service that predates central air. Before we specify anything we do a load calculation, look at the panel, and price the service upgrade honestly inside the same permit set. It is not glamorous, but it is the difference between a kitchen that works and one that trips.

faqs.q: How long will we be without a kitchen?
faqs.a: Plan on a couple of months of site work for a straightforward layout, longer when a wall comes out or the plan changes rooms. Custom cabinetry is the pacing item and is ordered months ahead so your house is not sitting open waiting on a delivery truck. We usually build a temporary kitchen somewhere sane, often the dining room or garage, and we tell you the honest date rather than the hopeful one.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen cost around here?
faqs.a: Your selections drive it more than the room's size does. Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the range, and a Victoria Park kitchen that also needs a structural opening, a service upgrade and relocated plumbing carries serious construction cost under the pretty part. We price against a written specification so you are comparing like for like. We are a high-end builder, not the lowest of three bids, and we would rather be clear about that at the walk-through.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos or open the door for us. Either way you get a specification, a schedule and a fixed price, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Victoria Park Bathroom Remodeling, Fort Lauderdale
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Victoria Park bath remodels in Fort Lauderdale replace 1930s plumbing before the marble ever arrives. Permitted and inspected. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Bathrooms built to outlast the pipes
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Victoria Park homes, with waterproofing tested before a single tile lands and every trade permitted and inspected through Fort Lauderdale Building Services. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Count the bathrooms in an original Victoria Park cottage and you will usually reach one. Houses along the older blocks near Victoria Courts and NE 7th Street were built when a single tiled bath served the whole family, and the fifties ranches added a second that is still four feet wide. The fix is almost always annexation: borrow a small bedroom, a hall closet or a screened porch and turn the result into a primary bath with two sinks, a real shower and somewhere to put a towel.

Bathroom permits are issued by the City of Fort Lauderdale through Development Services, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections along the way, all enforced under the Broward County amendments to the Florida Building Code that the Board of Rules and Appeals administers. The local complications are older than the code. Cast iron drains and galvanized supply lines are common in these houses, some sit on slab while others carry raised wood floors, and adding an exterior window for light means an HVHZ-approved impact unit rather than whatever matches.

Small room, zero forgiveness. Pans get flood-tested before tile, membranes get inspected instead of photographed, slopes get checked with a level, and exhaust gets ducted to the outside rather than into an attic where it will quietly ruin your framing. Every Victoria Park bath we build runs on a fixed written scope, daily supervision and protected pathways from your front door to the work zone. Licensed, insured and permitted on every job, with more than 20 years of South Florida work behind it.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: Inside a Victoria Park bath remodel
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Waterproofing and plumbing decide whether the marble was worth it. Here is what we scope in writing before a single tile is ordered.

scope_items.name: One less bedroom, one suite
scope_items.desc: Reworking bedrooms, closets and hallways into a genuine primary suite, with framing, plumbing rough-in and the permit drawings handled as one package.

scope_items.name: Pans that hold water
scope_items.desc: Sloped pans, linear or center drains, and membranes water-tested and signed off by an inspector before tile, because the only cheap leak is the one that never happens.

scope_items.name: Replacing what is behind
scope_items.desc: Cast iron and galvanized runs swapped for modern drain and supply while the walls are open, which never gets easier or cheaper than right now.

scope_items.name: Stone, glass and heat
scope_items.desc: Large-format slabs and tile set on properly prepared substrates, heavy frameless glass anchored into blocking that was put there on purpose, and heated floors where the build-up allows.

scope_items.name: Air that actually moves
scope_items.desc: Old houses vent badly, so the fan gets sized and ducted properly outdoors, and the light gets split between mirror, shower and room.

faqs.q: Can I put a curbless shower in a 1930s Victoria Park house?
faqs.a: The floor decides this, not the tile. On a slab we recess the pan by cutting concrete and rerouting drain lines, which is real work and gets priced as such. On a raised wood floor we drop framing to sink the pan instead. When neither is sensible, a low-profile curb with proper slope gives you nearly the same look and the same dry hallway. We tell you which one your house supports before you commit to an image.

faqs.q: The water pressure in my shower is terrible. Will a remodel fix it?
faqs.a: Partly, and the rest is not on your side of the meter. Interior galvanized supply lines corrode from the inside and choke flow, so replacing them while walls are open makes a genuine difference. Separately, the city has been replacing Victoria Park's original two-inch water mains with larger mains and new service connections, which improves supply pressure at the street. We check both and tell you which one is the problem.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit just to retile a bathroom?
faqs.a: Straight cosmetic replacement of tile and fixtures in the same locations is a lighter lift than people expect. The moment you move a drain, add a circuit, change the ventilation or open a wall, you are in permit territory through Fort Lauderdale Building Services with inspections before anything is covered. We pull the permits whenever the scope justifies it, because the inspection record is what protects you at resale.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house during a bathroom remodel?
faqs.a: If you have another working bath, yes, and most Victoria Park clients do exactly that. We build a dust wall, run protected pathways, keep the site tidy at the end of every day and work inside the hours the city noise ordinance allows. If the project is your only bathroom, we will say so plainly and help you plan around it rather than pretend six weeks of camping is fine.

faqs.q: What does a primary bath at this level cost?
faqs.a: The visible half is stone, glass and fittings, and it is not the half that surprises people. New drain and supply, waterproofing, framing repairs and ventilation sit underneath, and in a house from the thirties that work is rarely small. We walk the space, open what needs opening, and hand you a fixed written number rather than a range that quietly widens. High-end work priced honestly beats a low bid that meets your plumbing in week three.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_heading: The bathrooms, one at a time
bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the bath that annoys you most. We will scope it properly, price it honestly, and answer questions in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions for Victoria Park, Fort Lauderdale FL
home-additions.meta_description: Additions for Victoria Park homes in Fort Lauderdale: rear extensions, second stories, in-law suites. Engineered and permitted. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Room to stay on your street
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions and in-law suites on Victoria Park's tight platted lots. Engineered, zoned, permitted through the city, and supervised daily by a licensed South Florida general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house on a 1925 lot
intro_paragraphs: Alfred Kuhn platted Victoria Park in 1925 with curving and diagonal streets, which produced beautiful blocks and a fair number of awkward lots. Owners here rarely leave. They are minutes from Las Olas and a short walk from Holiday Park, so instead of moving they add: a rear family room and primary suite behind a cottage on NE 8th Street, a second story over a fifties ranch, a garage turned into a proper guest suite, or an in-law wing for parents who have decided Fort Lauderdale beats winter.

Fort Lauderdale's rules get specific once you add square footage, and the City's Development Services Department applies all of them at once. Zoning review under the city's land development regulations governs setbacks, lot coverage and the thirty-five-foot height limit that applies in the single-family districts covering most of Victoria Park. Structural drawings need an engineer, new openings need HVHZ product approvals, and work in a mapped flood zone brings an elevation certificate into the submittal. If your property sits in a special flood hazard area, the federal fifty-percent substantial improvement test can reshape the project, so we run that math before anyone draws.

New foundations next to ninety-year-old ones, tie-beams poured into walls that were never designed for them, roof tie-ins where stucco has to match a texture nobody makes anymore: that is the part of an addition you cannot see and cannot skip. PGX has delivered more than 150 remodels and additions across South Florida in over 20 years, all permitted and inspected. You get a fixed written scope, daily supervision, the occupied half of the house kept livable, and one accountable team from feasibility through warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with a survey, a zoning read and an engineer. These are the five shapes Victoria Park projects usually take.

scope_items.name: Rear extensions
scope_items.desc: Pushing the back of the house into the yard for a family room, a bigger kitchen or a primary suite, with the structure and roof tie-in engineered together.

scope_items.name: Going up a floor
scope_items.desc: Second stories on houses that were never meant to carry one, starting with an engineer's verdict on the existing walls, footings and lateral system.

scope_items.name: The garage, converted
scope_items.desc: Converting garages and carports into conditioned rooms with insulation, impact openings and legal mechanical extensions, permitted so the space is real square footage on paper.

scope_items.name: A suite for long stays
scope_items.desc: A bath, kitchenette and private entry for parents or grown children who are staying a while, sized to what the lot and the zoning actually allow.

scope_items.name: Ground you cannot see
scope_items.desc: New footings tied to old ones, underpinning where the soil demands it, tie-beam upgrades, and the flood-zone elevation work Fort Lauderdale checks before approving new floor area.

faqs.q: How big an addition will my Victoria Park lot allow?
faqs.a: That is a zoning question before it is a design question. The city's land development regulations set setbacks, maximum lot coverage and a thirty-five-foot height limit in the single-family districts, and the curving 1925 plat means plenty of lots here are not simple rectangles. We start with a current survey, read the zoning against it, and tell you the real envelope before anyone pays an architect to draw something that will not fit.

faqs.q: Does the FEMA fifty percent rule apply to my house?
faqs.a: Only if the property is in a mapped special flood hazard area, and in Fort Lauderdale that varies block by block. Where it applies, the rule compares your project cost against the structure's pre-improvement market value; cross the threshold and the whole building has to meet current floodplain requirements. The city will want an elevation certificate establishing where your finished floor actually sits. None of this is fatal, but it has to be settled before design, not at plan review.

faqs.q: Can a 1930s cottage take a second story?
faqs.a: Only a structural engineer can answer that, and the answer depends on what the walls are made of. Wood-framed cottages and hollow clay tile behave very differently from the concrete block of the fifties ranches, so the first spend is an evaluation of the existing walls and footings. Sometimes the honest recommendation is a rear extension instead, because it costs less and keeps you living in the house. We bring both options back with numbers attached.

faqs.q: There is a big oak where I want the addition. Can it be removed?
faqs.a: Maybe, and not casually. Tree removal in Fort Lauderdale takes a city permit, and whether replacement planting comes with it depends on the species, the size and the lot. In a neighborhood whose canopy is half its value, the smarter move is usually designing around the tree: shifting the footprint, adjusting the roofline, floating a deck clear of the roots. We check the tree before we check the budget.

faqs.q: How long from first conversation to finished room?
faqs.a: Most of the wait happens before construction. Survey, design, structural engineering, zoning review and permitting through LauderBuild routinely take months before a shovel moves, and building a substantial addition runs several more after that. A year from first meeting to furniture is a realistic frame, and second stories run longer. Every phase goes into a written schedule at estimate time, so there are no mystery months where nothing appears to be happening.

outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens and driveways for Victoria Park, Fort Lauderdale. Swale and right-of-way permits handled by a licensed GC. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Covered terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas and driveways for Victoria Park, built to HVHZ standards with city building and right-of-way permits pulled, inspections scheduled, and a supervisor on site every working day.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Oaks, swales and the water that follows
intro_paragraphs: The oak canopy over North and South Victoria Park Road is the neighborhood's best asset and its most annoying design constraint, which is why outdoor living here looks different from a bare-lot backyard. Lots are compact, so the work is precise: a covered terrace tucked behind a Mission-style cottage, a summer kitchen along a side yard, a pergola over a plunge pool, a re-laid driveway that finally drains. Homes along Lake Stranahan and the Karen Canal add dockside terraces and the seawall questions that come with them.

Outdoor projects in Victoria Park pull in more than one Fort Lauderdale desk. Structures need building permits through Development Services; summer kitchens need their own plumbing, gas and electrical permits; and anything touching the swale, apron or sidewalk needs an engineering right-of-way permit, with swale grading and sod restored to city standards. Pergolas and screen enclosures are engineered for HVHZ wind loads. On canal lots, seawall and dock work adds the city's marine review and a license from Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program.

April 2023 taught this neighborhood what standing water does to a house, and the city has been rebuilding Victoria Park's water mains and stormwater system since. We design terraces and driveways to move water away from the building, not toward the front door, and we coordinate around whatever the city has open in your street that month. Fixed written scope, permits pulled before work starts, a supervisor on site daily, and crews who keep a small lot tidy. We build under Lic. CGC1539072, licensed and insured.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terraces, kitchens, driveways and facades are one project, not five trades bumping into each other. Here is what we build and permit as a single scope.

scope_items.name: Roof over the terrace
scope_items.desc: Covered terraces and pergolas with footings, uplift connections and framing engineered for Broward wind loads, drawn to sit under the existing roofline naturally.

scope_items.name: The summer kitchen
scope_items.desc: Gas, water and power run and permitted properly, then cabinetry, counters and appliances chosen because they survive August outdoors, not because they photographed well.

scope_items.name: Driveways, aprons and swales
scope_items.desc: Pavers and finished concrete laid to drain, with the engineering right-of-way permit pulled and the swale regraded and sodded to the city's standard detail.

scope_items.name: Facades and finishes
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration on older cottages: cracked stucco cut out and patched to match texture, wood trim repaired or replaced, then a coating system that lasts.

scope_items.name: Impact doors and re-roof timing
scope_items.desc: HVHZ-approved terrace doors and windows installed in the right sequence with roofing work, so flashing, tie-ins and warranties all line up.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to redo my driveway in Victoria Park?
faqs.a: Yes, and probably two. The driveway itself is a building permit, and the apron where it crosses the swale to the street sits in the city right-of-way, which means an engineering permit and restoration of the swale to Fort Lauderdale's standard detail. The swale is not decoration; it is part of the drainage system, and the city cares about its grade. We file both and schedule them so the work is not sitting half-done.

faqs.q: The city is tearing up my street. Should I wait to start?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but we plan around it. Victoria Park has had watermain replacement, sewer lining and stormwater work running through it in phases, and that affects staging, deliveries, dumpster placement and sometimes water service for a day. We check the city's active project map for your block before we set a start date, and we coordinate with whoever is in the street rather than discovering them on a Monday morning.

faqs.q: My backyard floods. Can a terrace project fix the drainage?
faqs.a: It can help a great deal, and it is one of the first things we look at. Grading, slope away from the slab, permeable surfaces, French drains and properly sized inlets all belong in the design rather than added later as an apology. What a private terrace cannot do is fix a neighborhood-scale problem, which is exactly what the city's stormwater work is for. We will tell you which problem you have.

faqs.q: I have canal frontage. What is involved in replacing the seawall?
faqs.a: More agencies than you would like. Fort Lauderdale reviews seawall and dock work under its own waterway rules and now sets a minimum top elevation of five feet NAVD88 for new and substantially improved seawalls, aligned with Broward County's countywide standard. The county's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program licenses work in, on or under surface waters, and state or federal review can apply depending on location and scope. We coordinate the marine contractor and the approvals so the terrace and the seawall are one schedule, not two arguments.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a covered terrace and summer kitchen?
faqs.a: The structure and the utilities drive it. A paver terrace with lighting is one number; a roofed outdoor room with gas, water, power, appliances and stone counters is a different order of project, because there is engineering and permitting underneath the appliances. Selections then swing it further. We scope it in writing after walking the yard, so what you are comparing is a specification and a schedule, not a hopeful number per square foot.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: What the city file says about your house

The 1925 plat filled in with Mission cottages, Craftsman bungalows, small Mediterranean Revivals and postwar ranches, and almost every one of them has been altered since. A carport gets closed in. A jalousie porch becomes an air-conditioned den. A half bath appears where a closet used to be, a panel gets swapped on a Saturday. Plenty of it was permitted properly. The rest sits quietly in the address file until a title search, a lender or an insurance underwriter goes looking.

Permits and plan review for Victoria Park run through the City of Fort Lauderdale Development Services Department, where Building Services reads the drawings and sends the inspectors. Behind the city sits another layer: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which adopts the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the building officials and inspectors assigned to your job, and issues formal interpretations when a code section is disputed. All of Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. On lots the flood map puts near Lake Stranahan or Karen Canal, elevation and substantial-improvement rules join the same submittal.

We treat permitting as the first phase of construction, not a form somebody drops off downtown. PGX brings in the architect, engineer or surveyor a submittal genuinely requires, files complete instead of in installments, and answers plan review comments in writing so nothing rides on who happened to pick up the phone. A supervisor books each inspection and is standing in the house when the inspector arrives. What you keep afterward is a licensed contractor of record, a fixed written scope, and an address file that reads clean to the next buyer's attorney. Lic. CGC1539072, 20-plus years here, 150-plus projects, all permitted and inspected.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: Where Victoria Park files go wrong
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: From a single unclosed inspection to four decades of quiet alterations: we read the record, fix what it needs, and get the address signed off under a licensed general contractor.

scope_items.name: Open and expired permits
scope_items.desc: We pull the city's record for your address, work out what each open permit is actually missing, and carry it through reactivation, inspection and a documented final.

scope_items.name: After-the-fact permits
scope_items.desc: Legalizing the enclosed carport, the converted garage or the Florida room a prior owner added: as-built drawings, engineering where the structure calls for it, inspection of what stands.

scope_items.name: HVHZ windows and roofs
scope_items.desc: Impact units, doors and roof assemblies documented with approvals valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone and installed to the anchor detail those approvals actually cover.

scope_items.name: Zoning, flood and historic review
scope_items.desc: Setbacks, height and lot coverage checked early, elevation certificates where the flood map calls for them, and Historic Preservation Board approval on individually designated houses.

scope_items.name: Inspections to final sign-off
scope_items.desc: Trade inspections booked in the right order and attended by our supervisor, ending in a final that genuinely closes the permit instead of leaving it dormant.

faqs.q: Our closing is weeks away and the permit record is not clean. Where do we start?
faqs.a: With the file, not the house. Some entries are jobs abandoned halfway, some expired while the work sat, and plenty are jobs finished properly where nobody ever called the final inspection. That last kind usually ends with one visit and a closeout. The others can mean re-permitting, or opening finished work so an inspector can see what is behind it. Plan review moves in weeks rather than days, so start the moment the record surfaces.

faqs.q: Who issues permits for Victoria Park, and what does Broward County have to do with it?
faqs.a: Your permit comes from the City of Fort Lauderdale Development Services Department, where Building Services reviews the plans and assigns the inspectors. Broward then adds a county layer on top of the city. The Board of Rules and Appeals adopts the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies your building official and inspectors, and rules on disputed code language. You will never file anything with the Board yourself. Your contractor should still know those amendments cold, because Fort Lauderdale inspectors enforce them.

faqs.q: A previous owner enclosed the carport without a permit. Can that be legalized?
faqs.a: Usually, through an after-the-fact permit, and this neighborhood is full of the problem: enclosed carports, jalousie porches turned into cooled rooms, garages made into studios. We measure what stands, draw it as built, bring in an engineer where the framing or the beam over an opening needs one, and put it through inspection against the code in force today. Expect a wall or ceiling to be opened so connections can be seen, and expect the city to charge more for a permit that arrives after the work.

faqs.q: Do impact windows in Fort Lauderdale need special product approval?
faqs.a: Yes. Broward sits entirely inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every exterior opening and every roof assembly needs approval documentation valid here, and the installation has to match it down to anchor type, spacing and substrate. A window with the right approval and the wrong anchors fails inspection, which is how a schedule dies. On a 1930s elevation there is a second question worth asking early: profiles and sightlines that suit the house instead of flattening the front of it.

faqs.q: Does a 40-year style recertification apply to my Victoria Park house?
faqs.a: Not to a house. Broward County's Building Safety Inspection Program, enforced through the city's building official, runs on building age and size and exempts one- and two-family dwellings, so a detached cottage never enters it. Florida's milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies apply to condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories and up: here, the older low-rise buildings at the edges, not the houses on the numbered streets. If you sit on one of those boards, the repairs those reports call for are work we do.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Let us read the file first
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address. We will tell you plainly what the city still has open on it and what closing it out will take, in English o en español.
